prior_evidence: F307 same-placed gate bypass16 0/3, enabled16 3/3, reverse16 0/3, enabled17 3/3. Native delayed-start5us/50us 0/3 each. Prior recovered-clock ratio abnormal and repaired byPMA.

predictions.success_would_support: F307 request/ack and post-pulse diagnostic state are dispensable for present boot recovery.
predictions.failure_with_pulse_would_suggest: Functional ordering, clock-domain assumptions or implementation differences require review; no immediate attribution to handshake itself.

predictions.success_would_support: A1s post-RXRESETDONE wait is unnecessary in tested conditions; reinitializingPMA late in initial acquisition can suffice.
predictions.failure_with_pulse_would_suggest: A later timing window or RX/user-readiness state matters; PMA pulse presence alone is insufficient.
predictions.no_pulse_means: Invalid efficacy comparison; investigate timer/rearming/suppression before moreboot trials.

predictions.success_would_support: Changing native reset/user-clock wait may suffice without separatePMA logic.
predictions.confounds: Both reset hold and RXUSER wait change; separately compiled placement differs.
predictions.failure_would_suggest: Merely extending these native waits to5us is insufficient; not a disproof of all widths.

physical_cause_hypotheses: RX/PMA/CDR initial state or calibration depends on reset/clock ordering.
Board-specific rail/reference-clock startup or marginal analog conditions may predispose initial acquisition; not measured.
non_claims: CPLLLOCK/RXRESETDONE do not establish recovered-data/CDR correctness.
No jitter measurement or board rail waveform; no component-failure diagnosis.
PMA in sequential mode may reset downstream stages.
Latched pulse observations do not directly measure pulse count/duration.
Initialhold2-line alternative has different configuration-time qualification concern and is not counted as the minimum newPMA patch.
